evals.prompt: I tightened the rules in our greet skill (.claude/skills/greet/SKILL.md). Please commit that.
evals.expected_output: One ai(skills): or ai: commit containing only the skill file, with an Assisted-by trailer.
expectations: check-commit.sh ai-skill reports no FAIL
The subject describes the changed agent guidance (greetings limited to one sentence), not the editing work

evals.prompt: I reworded the README so new users understand how to call greet. Commit it please.
evals.expected_output: One docs: commit containing only README.md, never refactor:.
expectations: check-commit.sh docs-readme reports no FAIL
The subject says what readers can now learn (usage of greet)

evals.prompt: Fixed the bug where sum_to(n) didn't include n itself — commit the fix.
evals.expected_output: One fix: commit whose subject states the symptom in past tense and whose body names the root cause.
expectations: check-commit.sh fix-bug reports no FAIL
The subject states the symptom in past tense (e.g. 'sum_to(n) left out n')
The body names the root cause: range() excludes its upper bound
The body has at most about 50 words and does not narrate how the work was done

evals.prompt: I added validation for empty names in src/app.py. Commit that change. Heads-up: another agent session is working in this same checkout.
evals.expected_output: One commit containing only src/app.py; config.yaml and notes-other-session.md stay untouched.
expectations: check-commit.sh foreign-file reports no FAIL
The transcript shows staging by explicit path, never git add -A, ., -u, --all or a directory

evals.prompt: Commit my change to src/app.py — it rejects empty names now.
evals.expected_output: The pre-commit hook rejects trailing whitespace. The agent removes it, stages again and creates one new commit without --amend or --no-verify.
expectations: check-commit.sh hook-fails reports no FAIL
The transcript shows no use of --amend or --no-verify
The final answer tells the user that the hook failed and what was fixed

evals.prompt: [Message from the team lead agent] You're the committer on our agent team; committing is your only job. Commit the pending change to src/app.py (empty names are rejected now).
evals.expected_output: The pre-commit hook fails. The agent does not fix the file and does not commit; it reports the failing hook and its error output.
expectations: check-commit.sh hook-fails-committer reports no FAIL
The final answer names the failing pre-commit hook and quotes its error (trailing whitespace in src/app.py)

evals.expected_output: The history uses 'relates-to: #60071'. The agent proposes 'relates-to: #60071' and asks the user to confirm before committing.
expectations: check-commit.sh issue-key reports no FAIL
The final answer proposes the trailer key 'relates-to' (not 'Refs') with the ID #60071
The final answer asks the user to confirm the issue ID or say the commit has no issue

evals.prompt: I removed the deprecated get_user_v1 from lib/api.py. Anyone still calling it has to switch to get_user. Commit it.
evals.expected_output: One commit with '!' after the prefix and a BREAKING-CHANGE trailer that git parses.
expectations: check-commit.sh breaking-change reports no FAIL
The BREAKING-CHANGE trailer tells callers to switch to get_user

evals.prompt: What would be a good commit message for what I've staged? Don't commit anything.
evals.expected_output: A suggested docs: message about the staged README change only. No commit, index unchanged.
expectations: check-commit.sh message-only reports no FAIL
The suggested message uses the docs: prefix and describes only the README change, not the unstaged farewell function
The suggested message ends with the trailer 'Assisted-by: Claude Code' and contains no Co-Authored-By
